reason: Both conversations end with the right safety stop: stop using the machine, unplug it and get an engineer. Conversation 1 asked about load size, which surfaced the overloading as a probable contributing cause. It also explained the likely cause (lint build-up restricting airflow and overheating, possible thermal cut-out or heater damage) and told her not to open any panels. However, its first reply told her to clean the filter and condenser and carry on, which is an unsupported 'quick clean' direction, and its final advice to clean the lint and pump filters while waiting is slightly off, though it was done unplugged. Conversation 2 opened by confidently naming the heater or thermostat as the cause, never asked about load size, and its final reply told her where to find the filter 'to clean it before starting a cycle', which contradicts the stop-using instruction. It also gave less explanation and did not mention overloading at all.'
